title.value: Deformation Mechanisms, Structural Architecture, and Petrophysical Properties a Large Normal Fault in Massive Platform Carbonates, Fucino Area, Cetral Italy

note.value:
We studied the structural arrangement of the footwall of a large, basin-bounding normal fault that juxtaposes continental sediments against massive platform carbonates. Based on the crosscutting and abutting relationships, we distinguished the structural elements that make up the grain of the limestone host rock from those related to normal faulting. We propose a conceptual model of fault development in which normal faulting initiated with shearing of the preexisting weaknesses of the host rock and formation and interaction of several sets of joints, veins, pressure solution seams, and subsequent throughgoing slip surfaces. Concurrent uplift and evolution of the basin on the hanging wall localized the deformation at the hanging wall-footwall contact, widening the fault core, and pulverizing the adjacent limestone in the damage zone. The last stages of faulting were characterized by slip along the main slip surface(s), formation of cataclastic shear bands within the pulverized limestone, and diffuse brittle deformation in the damage zone.

Based on the intensity of deformation, we distinguish three main sub-components within the damage zone, which are, the pulverized, intensely fractured, and moderately fractured limestone, respectively. We mapped the extension of the fault core and these three sub-components of the damage zone to characterize the lateral variability of the structural architecture and assess the permeability structure of the Venere fault. The fault core comprises both cement- and matrix-supported fault rocks with low porosity and permeability, and thus forms a barrier to cross-fault fluid flow. Based on the capillary presure of the matrix- supported fault rocks, they form a class C seal ,trapping up to 77 m of gas and 140 m of oil. The pulverized limestone that flanks the fault core also forms a barrier to fluid flow because of the cataclastic shear bands present in this rock. Conversely, both fractured limestones of the damage zone comprise matrices with high porosity and permeability and small faults and form conduits to cross- and along-fault fluid flow. The central part of the fault is characterized by well-developed fault core and damage zone and it is thus associated with a combined barrier-conduit permeability structure. On the contrary, the fault forms a localized conduit for fluid flow in correspondence of the southern tip, where the fault core thins out and the limestone of the damage zone is fractured but not pulverized.

Agosta, Fabrizio and Aydin, Atilla. (2005). Deformation Mechanisms, Structural Architecture, and Petrophysical Properties a Large Normal Fault in Massive Platform Carbonates, Fucino Area, Cetral Italy. Stanford Digital Repository. Available at: http://purl.stanford.edu/cq085bm7304
